messages:
ravi: Quick note: the Go SDK generator sample app can hang if auth refresh happens mid-stream. Repro with short token TTL + retry path + caller cancel.

ana: Ack, reproduced locally. The sample's retry goroutine uses `context.Background()` so cancellation doesn't flow and the caller blocks on a range over the Events channel.

jo: Two fixes: (1) change SDK streaming surface so callers use an explicit Recv(ctx) + Close() pattern instead of range-over-channel, (2) update sample to avoid Background() in goroutines and show the token-ttl child-context pattern.

ravi: Minimal problematic snippet I used:```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(req.Context(), 4*time.Second)
defer cancel()
g := sdk.NewGenerator(c)
stream := g.Start(ctx, req) // Start returns Events() chan
for ev := range stream.Events() { fmt.Println(ev.Text) }
```
If refresh triggers a retry the Events channel is never closed.

jo: Proposed API: add Stream(ctx, req) -> (*GenStream, error). GenStream has Recv(ctx) (Chunk, error), Close() error (idempotent), Done() <-chan struct{}. Keep old API as a shim and deprecate later.

ana: Sample guidance to include: create a child context tied to token TTL and defer stream.Close(); example:```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(reqCtx, 10*time.Second)
defer cancel()
str, err := gen.Stream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { return err }
defer str.Close()
for {
  ch, err := str.Recv(ctx)
  if err == io.EOF { break }
  if err != nil { return err }
  fmt.Print(ch.Text)
}
```
This ensures Recv returns quickly on ctx cancel.

jo: Also add an e2e that simulates mid-stream auth refresh (short TTL + forced refresh) and asserts no goroutine leaks after Close. Consider a sample-lint rule that flags `context.Background()` usage in long-lived goroutines.

ravi: I'll open a PR with the shim + updated sample + e2e tests and tag for the next devex sprint. Will include migration notes.

ci-bot: Created issue SDK-2607: "Go SDK: generator streaming - explicit cancellation API and sample fixes" and added a draft changelog entry.
